name: dharma
definition: Duty, ethical order and the way of living that sustains life; its meaning depends on context.

name: karma
definition: Action, and the consequences of action in teachings about moral cause and effect.

name: Atman · ātman
definition: The Self; schools differ in their account of its relationship to ultimate reality.

name: brahman
definition: Ultimate reality in Upanishadic and Vedantic thought. Brahman is distinct from Brahma, the creator deity.

name: Moksha · mokṣa
definition: Liberation from samsara, the cycle of rebirth; its nature is understood differently across schools.

name: bhakti
definition: Devotion and loving dedication to the Divine.

name: Shakti · śakti
definition: Power or energy; divine power, especially the Goddess in Shakta traditions.

name: deva
definition: A divine being or god; the feminine form is devi.

name: Devi · devī
definition: Goddess; also a title for the Divine Mother.

name: tapas
definition: Spiritual discipline and austerity, associated with inward effort and transformation.

name: yantra
definition: A diagram or device; in worship, a geometric form associated with a deity and contemplation.

name: Purana · purāṇa
definition: A genre of sacred narrative including divine stories, cosmology, genealogies and teachings.

name: Jyotirlinga · jyotirliṅga
definition: A radiant form of Shiva’s linga, associated with sacred shrines. The Shiva Purana’s Kotirudra Samhita names twelve principal jyotirlingas.

name: Itihasa · itihāsa
definition: Traditional narrative of the past; in this guide, the epic literature of the Ramayana and Mahabharata. Itihasa is named alongside Purana in Chandogya Upanishad 7.1.2.

name: Brahmastra · brahmāstra
definition: A divine weapon associated with Brahma. In Sundara Kanda 48, Indrajit uses Brahma’s weapon to bind Hanuman.

name: Linga · liṅga
definition: An emblem or sign; in Shaiva worship, the linga is a sacred form through which Shiva is worshipped.

name: Avatar · avatāra
definition: A divine descent or manifestation, especially in traditions of Vishnu. Bhagavad Gita 4.6–8 discusses Krishna’s manifestation and its purpose.

name: Asura · asura
definition: A class of beings who may cooperate with or oppose the devas in sacred narratives. In Bhagavata Purana 8.7, devas and asuras take part in the ocean churning.

name: Akshara · akṣara
definition: The imperishable. In Gargi’s dialogue with Yajnavalkya, it names the reality that does not pass away; in other contexts, akshara can also mean a syllable or letter.

name: Shreyas · śreyas
definition: The truly beneficial or lasting good. In the Katha Upanishad, Yama distinguishes shreyas from what is merely pleasant.

name: Preyas · preyas
definition: What is immediately pleasant or attractive. The Katha Upanishad contrasts preyas with shreyas, the path of lasting good.

name: Sat
definition: Being, existence or the Real. In Chandogya Upanishad 6, Sat is taught as the one reality from which beings arise, by which they live and into which they return.

name: Tat Tvam Asi · tat tvam asi
definition: “That you are,” the teaching repeated by Uddalaka to Shvetaketu in Chandogya Upanishad 6. Vedanta traditions interpret the relationship expressed by these words in different ways.

name: Akasha · ākāśa
definition: Space, sky or the vast expanse. Its philosophical range depends on context; in Gargi’s questioning, the worlds are described as woven in akasha.

name: Shraddha · śraddhā
definition: Trust, reverent confidence or faithful resolve. It can describe the inward seriousness that turns a person toward a teaching or sacred undertaking.

name: Vidya · vidyā
definition: Knowledge, learning or insight. In spiritual contexts it may refer to knowledge that dispels ignorance, though its precise meaning varies by text and school.

name: Avidya · avidyā
definition: Ignorance or misapprehension, especially regarding the Self and reality. Hindu philosophical schools explain its nature and removal differently.

name: Prana · prāṇa
definition: Vital breath or life force. The word can name breath, vitality or a particular life-function depending on the teaching in which it appears.

name: Samsara · saṃsāra
definition: The continuing cycle of birth, death and rebirth from which moksha is liberation; traditions explain this cycle and liberation in different ways.

name: Shruti · śruti
definition: The Vedic corpus regarded as heard or revealed in the tradition; the Upanishads belong to it.

name: Smriti · smṛti
definition: Remembered textual tradition, a broad grouping including epics and Puranas.

name: Samhita · saṃhitā
definition: A collection; in Vedic study, hymn and mantra collections are distinguished from the associated Upanishads.

name: Rishi · ṛṣi
definition: A sage or seer, approached through particular textual settings and lineages.

name: Guna · guṇa
definition: A quality of nature; sattva, rajas and tamas are discussed in Bhagavata Purana 11.25.

name: Purushartha · puruṣārtha
definition: An aim of human life, traditionally understood through dharma, artha, kama and moksha.

name: Darshana · darśana
definition: A philosophical school or perspective; the six classical systems differ in methods and conclusions.

name: Kalpa · kalpa
definition: A cycle identified as a day of Brahma in Bhagavata Purana 3.11.

name: Manvantara · manvantara
definition: The period of a Manu, discussed in Bhagavata Purana 3.11 and 8.13–14.

name: Loka · loka
definition: A world or realm; Bhagavata Purana 2.5 describes seven upper and seven lower Lokas.

name: Yuga · yuga
definition: An age in a recurring cycle: Krita, Treta, Dvapara and Kali in Bhagavata Purana 3.11.

name: Sarga · sarga
definition: Primary creation, among the characteristics named for a Purana in Bhagavata 12.7.
